analysis.title: Margin-Call-Related Selling Takes Gold Back to Its Fair-Value
key_insights: Gold fell 3.7% on Friday with no obvious catalyst. Yields and the dollar were lower, so the author attributes the move to raising cash to cover losses elsewhere and to CTA selling as long-term momentum signals turned negative.
The SOX had its 41st worst decline in over 30 years the same day, centered on semiconductor stocks, which the author links to the cash-raising in gold.
The decline took gold below the author's fair value for the first time since 2023. The model uses real yields, the dollar, the S&P and copper on a year-over-year basis.
The author expects the move back under fair value to provide a durable base for a gradual price recovery.

The fundamental reasons to own gold are unchanged from last year. Inflationary and deflationary tail-risks are elevated because of large persistent fiscal deficits, high financial system leverage and the weaponisation of the dollar.
Gold behaved like a meme stock during the rally. The author says the hot money has largely left, and much of it is now nursing losses in US and Korean tech stocks.
US retail has not capitulated, judged by US gold ETF flows. Gold ETFs are only 1.8% of above-ground stocks, so the author argues the focus on ETFs is excessive.

Investors in China and the rest of Asia bought before US and European investors early in the rally. They did not sell earlier this year, based on flows into Asia-domiciled gold ETFs, while US ETF outflows rose.
Gold was lower again on the day of writing (Wednesday, Nov 4).

macro_indicators.interpretation: The author reads the drop as forced cash-raising and CTA selling, not a change in gold's fundamentals.
The author uses the prior rally as the reference for when gold last traded below fair value.

risk_factors: Further forced selling in gold if equity losses, especially in semiconductors, continue.
US retail ETF holders have not yet capitulated, so more selling is possible.
Gold was lower again on the day of writing.
Momentum signals for CTAs have turned negative.
